 celebrity health What to Know About ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor RJ Mitte’s Cause of Death and Cerebral Palsy Diagnosis
 The actor, who was best-known for his role as Walter “Flynn” White Jr. on “Breaking Bad,” lived with cerebral palsy. His mother reveals what she saw in the months before his death. Updated   Oct. 16, 2026, 9:38 AM EDT / Source : TODAY A. Pawlowski
 RJ Mitte, Known for 'Breaking Bad' Role, Dies at 34 00:30 Share Add TODAY to Google RJ Mitte was one of the emotional centers of “Breaking Bad,” playing a teenager with cerebral palsy, a condition he lived with in real life since he was a toddler.
 The actor and disability rights advocate died by suicide at 34, his representatives said. A celebration of life will be held on Friday, Oct. 16, in Brownsville, Texas, where Mitte lived, according to his obituary .
 Mitte was going through an emotional time, but friends and family had no indication he might end his own life, his mother, Dyna Mitte, told NBC News in an exclusive interview.
 “For the last three months, I’d been offering for him to go to therapy, trying to get him to go there, but he was like, ‘No, I’ve got it. It’s OK. I’m handling it,’” his mother said.
 If she could go back, she would have dragged him “screaming and yelling” to a counselor, she said.
 Her son had no history of mental illness and never saw a therapist, she noted, but a close friend told her Mitte had mentioned some issues “that he was very hurt over.” She declined to share details.
 “We all go through some heartbreak in our life and, and we all deal with it differently,” Dyna Mitte told NBC News. “If I had known anything and could have done anything different, I truly would have. I would have given my life for his life.”
 She said one of the hardest aspects of coping with her son’s death was that it doesn’t appear he left a note. She believes ending his life may have been a “spur of the moment” decision.
 “I just want him to be remembered for all the wonderful things he’s done in life, and all the people he’s impacted,” Dyna Mitte said.
 RJ Mitte’s Cause of Death 
 Mitte died on Monday, Oct. 12, in Brownsville, Texas. His mother found him.
 “Sadly, we can confirm that suicide was the cause of death,” Sean Reilly, his representative, said in a statement to NBC News on Tuesday, Oct. 13.
 The “beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate” lived with cerebral palsy and drew from his own experience to bring authenticity to his “Breaking Bad” role and build “a platform on disability awareness and inclusion,” his reps added .
 Nonprofit United Cerebral Palsy said it was “heartbroken by the loss” of Mitte, who was an ambassador for organization, noting his death was “deeply felt across the disability community.”
 “We knew him as someone who brought kindness, humor, and genuine warmth to every interaction,” said Susan Sellers, president and CEO of UCP, in a statement .
 ‘Breaking Bad’ Co-stars React 
 Bryan Cranston, who played Mitte’s father on “Breaking Bad” from 2008 to 2013, wrote in an Instagram post that he was in “deep despair.” He recalled Mitte was 14 when he was cast as his son, a role “he played with joy and enthusiasm.”
 “Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never — ever — allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything. He met the demanding shooting schedule head on with great determination,” Cranston wrote .
 Anna Gunn said she was lucky to play Mitte’s mother on the hit TV show and called him her “beloved TV son.”
 “He was doggedly determined that his disability would not impede him, but would instead give him the opportunity to enlighten and educate others,” Gunn said in a statement to People .
 “I was so proud of him; we all were.”
 Co-star Aaron Paul said he called Mitte “Superman” because he always led with kindness and strength. The actor urged others to say something if they’re struggling.
 “RJ, you have always been an inspiration for so many. I am so sorry you were hurting my friend. I wish we knew,” Paul wrote on Instagram .
 “You were born into a world with challenges but you never let any of that stand in your way... What an absolute tragic loss.”
 What RJ Mitte Said About His Cerebral Palsy 
 The actor was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at around 3 years old, and underwent physical, occupational and speech therapy, he told Vice in 2016.
 “People perceive disability as a weakness, as an illness, as something that needs to be cured, and we have to fight against that,” Mitte noted. “Someone said, ‘What’s wrong with you?’ And I was like, ‘What’s wrong with me? What’s wrong with you? I’m fine, man.’”
 As a child, Mitte was a severe toe walker so part of the treatment involved doctors bending his foot as far as it would go and putting it in a cast, “which was not fun,” he recalled. A few weeks later, the cast would be taken off, his foot bent even further and immobilized in a cast again — a process that was repeated until his foot was flat.
 “I’m always working at taking control. It’s a fight. It will always be a fight,” he said about his body.
 Mitte loved exercise and playing sports. He ran, lifted weights and played soccer to keep his body flexible and reduce stress, he told BrainHealth.com .
 “One thing I’ve learned from my disability is that when there is an obstacle, you adapt and grow. You can’t let that obstacle break you down and discourage you,” he said.
 “Breaking Bad” showed real characters that everyone could relate to, Mitte noted. He played the son of Walter White — a high school chemistry teacher who starts making and selling crystal meth as a way to secretly make more money for his family after he’s diagnosed with terminal cancer.
 Mitte’s teenage character was based on a real person with cerebral palsy who was friends with the show’s creator, Mitte said on The Joe Vulpis Podcast a week before his death.
 The actor kept the forearm crutches his character used in “Breaking Bad.” That was the only thing he “truly wanted” from the set, Mitte said, though he didn’t use them in real life.
 The actor was reluctant to become an advocate at first, but found himself naturally doing advocacy work. He created an anti-bullying campaign and took part in philanthropic work.
 “I’m lucky that I can be an advocate, I’m lucky that I can do what I do. … I think we all have an obligation to have an impact for the positive,” he said.
 Mitte understood the power of visibility, United Cerebral Palsy said, noting that “when entertainment, education, and public life represent people with disabilities authentically, it can challenge stereotypes and expand what others believe is possible.”
 Asked how people with disabilities can remove the stigma of not being able-bodied, Mitte urged others to be open.
 “Don’t hide your disability. Don’t hide whatever it is that you’re hiding — and I’m not just talking about a physical disability, I’m talking about a mental disability. Show who you are and what you are to the world,” he said.
 In 2025, the actor got engaged to his longtime girlfriend after he proposed during a fundraising gala for United Cerebral Palsy of San Diego, People reported .
 “I’m thrilled to have found my person, my partner in life who makes me want to be better, no matter what we’re doing,” he said about his engagement.
 What Is Cerebral Palsy? 
 It’s a group of neurologic disorders caused when a baby’s brain is damaged, usually as it develops in the womb, disrupting a child’s ability to control muscles and movement, and maintain posture and balance, according to the National Library of Medicine .
 While most people with cerebral palsy have the condition at birth, it may not be diagnosed until months or years later, the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke explains.
 Symptoms depend on how the condition affects the body — it can cause arm or leg weakness, stiff muscles, involuntary movements and other problems.
 There are many different types and levels of disability, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention .
 “A person with severe CP might need to use special equipment to be able to walk or might not be able to walk at all and might need lifelong care,” the CDC notes.
 “A person with mild CP, on the other hand, might walk a little awkwardly, but might not need any special help.”
 Mitte had mild cerebral palsy and stopped wearing leg braces at 13, he told L.A. Parent . But his character in “Breaking Bad” used forearm crutches.
 There’s no cure for cerebral palsy, but treatment such as physical therapy, medication, surgery and mobility devices can help people manage their symptoms.
 If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or chat live at 988lifeline.org . You can also visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional support.
